description: Fruit, nut and perennial vegetables. minZone = NRCan hardiness zone where reliably hardy. Marginal = your zone equals minZone (at its limit). yieldKgPerPlant is a mature-plant estimate.

records.name: Haskap (U of Sask. 'Borealis', 'Indigo Gem')
records.pollinatorPartner: Two compatible varieties, e.g. 'Indigo Gem' + 'Honey Bee'
records.notes: Earliest fruit of the year (June). Very cold hardy. Blooms early but flowers survive −7 °C.

records.name: Saskatoon ('Thiessen', 'Smoky')
records.notes: Native relative grows wild on the Shield. Watch for birds and cedar-apple rust.

records.name: Rhubarb ('Canada Red')
records.notes: Stalks only — leaves are poisonous (oxalic acid). Lasts decades.

records.name: Apple 'Norland'
records.pollinatorPartner: Any other apple or a crabapple such as 'Dolgo'
records.rootstock: Antonovka seedling (standard, very hardy) or Siberian crab (Malus baccata) in zone 2–3
records.notes: Early, hardy prairie apple. Short storage life.

records.name: Apple 'Goodland'
records.rootstock: Antonovka or Bud 118 (zone 3); Ottawa 3 dwarf is marginal below zone 4
records.notes: Stores 2–3 months. Good all-purpose apple.

records.name: Apple 'Honeycrisp'
records.pollinatorPartner: Another apple blooming at the same time
records.notes: Excellent keeper but less hardy.

records.name: Crabapple 'Dolgo'
records.notes: Universal pollinator for apples. Superb for jelly and pectin.

records.name: Pear 'Ure'
records.rootstock: Ussurian pear (Pyrus ussuriensis), hardy to zone 2
records.notes: Small sweet pears; one of the hardiest.

records.name: Pear 'Golden Spice'
records.notes: Good pollinator for 'Ure'. Best cooked or canned.

records.name: Plum 'Pembina'
records.rootstock: Prunus nigra (Canada plum) or P. americana
records.notes: Large red plum.

records.name: Plum 'Toka'
records.notes: Best pollinator for hybrid plums.

records.name: Sour cherry 'Carmine Jewel' (U of Sask.)
records.notes: Bush cherry, own-root: comes back true if frozen to the ground.

records.name: Sour cherry 'Evans'
records.notes: Tart pie cherry, very productive.

records.name: Nanking cherry
records.notes: Fast, tough hedge fruit.

records.name: Apricot 'Westcot'
records.notes: Blooms very early: spring frosts often kill the crop. Plant on a north slope to delay bloom.

records.name: Black currant 'Titania'
records.notes: Very high vitamin C. Choose white pine blister rust-resistant varieties (white pine is common on the Shield).

records.name: Red currant 'Red Lake'
records.notes: Shade tolerant. Jelly.

records.name: Gooseberry 'Pixwell'
records.notes: Nearly thornless.

records.name: Raspberry 'Boyne' (summer)
records.notes: Canadian-bred, very hardy. Spreads by suckers. Yield per metre of row.

records.name: Strawberry 'Kent' (June-bearing)
records.notes: Canadian (AAFC). Mulch with straw for winter.

records.name: Half-high blueberry ('Northblue' + 'Northcountry')
records.notes: Needs acidic soil pH 4.5–5.5: many Shield soils already are. Lowbush blueberries grow wild here.

records.name: Highbush cranberry (Viburnum trilobum)
records.notes: Native. Tart fruit holds on the bush into winter: emergency food.

records.name: Elderberry ('Adams' or native S. canadensis)
records.notes: Cook berries — raw berries, stems and leaves are toxic.

records.name: Sea buckthorn
records.notes: Extremely high vitamin C and oil. Thorny; suckers.

records.name: Asparagus 'Mary Washington'
records.notes: Plant crowns; first real harvest year 3. Lasts 20 years.

records.name: Jerusalem artichoke (sunchoke)
records.notes: Calorie tubers dug any time the ground is soft. Very invasive: plant where it can't spread. Causes gas.

records.name: Horseradish
records.notes: Spreads aggressively.

records.name: Egyptian walking onion
records.notes: Perennial onion; greens early spring.

records.name: Chives
records.notes: First green of spring.

records.name: Beaked hazelnut (native)
records.notes: Native nut; harvest before squirrels.

records.name: Butternut (Juglans cinerea)
records.notes: Native but endangered (butternut canker): wild trees are protected under Ontario's Endangered Species Act. Plant certified tolerant stock.

records.name: Grape 'Valiant'
records.notes: Hardiest common grape. Juice and jelly.

records.name: Arctic kiwi (Actinidia kolomikta)
records.notes: Grape-sized fruit, very high vitamin C.

records.name: Hardy kiwi 'Issai' (A. arguta)
records.notes: Self-fertile but bears more with a male.

records.name: Chokecherry (native)
records.notes: Cook and strain — pits, leaves and stems contain cyanide compounds.

records.name: Mulberry 'Illinois Everbearing'
records.notes: Too tender for most of Northern Ontario.

records.name: Peach 'Reliance'
records.notes: Southern Ontario only.

records.name: Sweet cherry 'Stella'
records.notes: Southern Ontario only.
